key_insight: Physics-guided deep learning estimates 3D bubble position and physical-equivalent diameter from single-camera shadowgraphs without stereoscopic hardware.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a scalable diagnostic for bubble size and spatial distributions that govern transport and uniformity in dense multiphase flows.
method: Render DNS-resolved bubbles with validated Monte Carlo ray tracing at multiple focal settings.
Preprocess bubble crops and train a focal-coordinate-conditioned multitask network to predict signed depth and diameter.
Evaluate on timestamp-separated synthetic data, closed-loop DNS reconstruction, and experimental images.
evidence_signal: Using 900 frames and 87,728 labeled instances, the study reports ~97.6% normalized depth accuracy on held-out data, <9.71% diameter error in a 180-bubble DNS test, and 68–92% experimental diameter-PDF overlap.
watch_item: Reconstruction errors increase with distance from the focal plane, limiting the depth range over which bubbles can be reliably recovered.
paper_title: Monocular 3D bubble reconstruction: DNS-informed ray tracing and deep learning
